subject.title: Feature Request: Add channel creation to message tool

question: Should OpenClaw expose agent-driven channel creation for bundled Slack and Discord integrations, and if so, what explicit operator opt-in, provider-scope validation, and default-off discovery policy is required?
rationale: Creating channels changes workspace/server structure and may use privileged bot or user credentials; source history establishes an implementation seam but not the product-security authority contract.

options.title: Approve a default-off provider contract
options.body: Authorize Slack and Discord plugins to advertise and execute channel creation only behind an explicit per-account admin-action gate with required scope diagnostics and focused live proof.

options.title: Limit scope to Discord CLI wiring
options.body: Land only the existing Discord CLI gap while leaving Slack channel creation and the cross-provider administrative contract out of scope.

options.title: Defer workspace administration
options.body: Keep the action unavailable until maintainers define a broader policy for agent-initiated workspace and server mutations.

recommendation.title: Approve a default-off provider contract
recommendation.body: Authorize Slack and Discord plugins to advertise and execute channel creation only behind an explicit per-account admin-action gate with required scope diagnostics and focused live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current issue discussion and area history connect this person most directly to the message-action and plugin-boundary decision surface.
